a microfluidics‐based approach for synthesis of visible light active nanomaterials and inline photocatalytic reactor can be employed to enhance the photocatalytic performance and the antibacterial efficacy of the synthesized nanophotocatlysts.

the development of microreactor‐assisted synthesis of visible light active nanoparticles and their application in inline photocatalysis.
the development of a continuous flow microreactor for the controlled synthesis of visible light active nanocatalyst and inline photocatalysis.
the development of a microfluidic platform to prepare visible light active Ag 2 S nanoparticles and to evaluate their photocatalytic activity in the inline microchannel.

the microreactors are very efficient and promising tools in the synthesis of nanophotocataclysts and inline photocatalysis.

the microreactor‐integrated photocatalytic process is an efficient and cost‐effective approach to synthesize and employ visible‐light active nanomaterials for inline photocatalysis and antibacterial activity.

the present study demonstrates that microfluidics‐based continuous synthesis of nanomaterials is an effective approach for the controlled synthesis of nanomaterals with enhanced photocatalytic activity and also for inline photocatalysis of organic dye.
